_comment: TEMPLATE. Copy this to .report_info.json and replace the placeholder text:
cp report_info.example.json .report_info.json
generate_compact_report.py reads .report_info.json from its output directory
and renders the blocks underneath the interop matrix. That file is
gitignored, so the published wording is not versioned; this template is,
so the expected shape stays documented. A missing .report_info.json is not
an error: the matrix renders on its own and the script notes it on stderr.
Each entry in "blocks" becomes one card, laid out in a two-column grid in
the order given. A block has a "title" plus any combination of:
body    Paragraph text. A string, or a list of strings joined with a
single space so long prose can be line-wrapped for editing.
This is the ONLY field inserted as raw HTML, so inline tags
such as <strong> and <em> work here. Keep it to inline
formatting; anything untrusted must not go in this file.
Note: because it is raw HTML, angle brackets are read as tags
— placeholders below use [square brackets] for that reason.
links   Buttons below the body. "label" and "href" are required;
"icon" optionally names a built-in glyph (see LINK_ICONS in
the script; "github" is the only one today). http, https and
mailto URLs only — anything else is dropped with a warning.
legend  Status key rows. "outcome" names a pytest result (Passed,
Failed, Error, Skipped) and pulls in the exact same glyph the
matrix cells use, so the key cannot drift from the table.
Blocks are free-form: rename them, drop them, or add your own.

blocks.title: About this report
body: [What generated these results, and what was tested against.
One or two sentences. Inline emphasis works here.]

legend.description: [Optional: drop this entry if runs never skip.]

blocks.title: Reading the matrix
body: [How to interpret rows, columns and sections. Rows are agents,
columns are wallets; a wallet with an extra parametrize dimension

blocks.title: [Your own block]
body: [Caveats, contact details, how to report a wrong result —
whatever suits the audience of the published page.]
